newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Northland extends consultation on Marsden.
newsitem.headline: Northland extends consultation on Marsden.

text.p: Northland Port Corporation (NZ) Ltd said on Friday it was allowing more time for consultations with Maori groups over its Marsden Point Deepwater Port project.

Chairman Jim Hardie said a board meeting had approved a request from Northland Regional Council to allow more time for iwi consultations, after some iwi groups were concerned they had not been adequately represented in the consultation process.

Hardie said the deadline for submissions on the project officially closed last November and independent commissioners appointed by Northland Regional Council and Whangarei District Council were due to start hearing those submissions in March.
Hardie said Northland Port had now agreed to delay the hearings until June.

The company filed resource applications last June to build a NZ$50 million wharf at Marsden Point. The facility is to be built near the existing deepwater oil wharves serving the Marsden Point oil refinery at the entrance to Whangarei Harbour.
